correctness.rationale: For horizon n objective epsilon_n|x| with epsilon_n=theta b sqrt(H_n)/S_n, sign(0)=0, eta_t=gamma/sqrt(t), and iid bounded Rademacher noise (b-epsilon_n)xi_t, early normalized noise up to m_n=floor(n/(log n)^4) has CLT variance H_m/H_n->1 while early drift epsilon_n S_m/(b sqrt(H_n))=theta S_m/S_n->0. Late drift has total normalized mass ->theta, late noise supremum variance O((H_n-H_m)/H_n)->0 by Doob. A deterministic bounded-disturbance tracking estimate then gives normalized last iterate convergence to -soft_theta(Z), not a Gaussian itself. Normalized objective ->gamma b² theta/2 (|Z|-theta)_+, with mean gamma b² theta[phi(theta)-theta barPhi(theta)] from uniform L2 moments. Root uniqueness follows theta barPhi(theta)/phi(theta) increasing 0->1 and crossing 1/2. Independent 100,000 random finite bounded-disturbance trajectories satisfied the claimed 3delta+h tracking bound; numerical unique theta*=0.612003180962481, coefficient 0.10122824509401235. The finite checks corroborate but do not prove the triangular-array CLT/limit.
residual_risks: Objective and independent oracle distribution vary with horizon n; this is not one fixed objective weak limit.
The zero atom is a weak-limit mass, not asserted as a finite-n exact atom.

value.rationale: The Gaussian-to-soft-threshold transition yields a point mass at the minimizer, explicit exceedance curve, exact expected error and unique optimal within-family tuning. It refines an established lower bound in a mathematically natural way and quantifies stochastic subgradient dynamics, not just another big-O rate.
residual_risks: The theorem is restricted to a tuned family; the optimum is not a global minimax optimum.

scientific_limitations: Scalar absolute value with horizon-dependent curvature and noise, asymptotic n->infinity.
